conceptual assets.concept: Decoded shift command (instruction decode / start decision)
conceptual assets.reasoning: RTL computes a module-local command signal from the control bus and uses it to start or gate all shift activity. Explicit: "valid_cmd <= '1' when (ctrl_i.alu_cp_alu = '1') and (...) else '0'". Serial flow: "if (valid_cmd = '1') then shifter.busy <= '1'; ... shifter.cnt <= shamt_i; shifter.sreg <= rs1_i;". Barrel flow: bs_level(0) and bs_sign are driven only when valid_cmd='1' and "valid_o <= valid_cmd". Corrupting this decision changes whether/when the shifter loads, runs, or reports results, establishing an integrity requirement. The decision is produced here (valid_cmd) from the input control port (ctrl_i).

conceptual assets.concept: Shift operand value (the data word to be shifted)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The value to be shifted enters the block and is stored/propagated by the shifter logic. Serial: on start "shifter.sreg <= rs1_i" and serial updates shift shifter.sreg each cycle; serial outputs use "res_o <= shifter.sreg when (shifter.done_ff = '1') else (others => '0')". Barrel: "bs_level(0) <= ... bit_rev_f(rs1_i) ... else rs1_i" and then "bs_result <= bs_level(bs_level'left)" is registered and used to form res_o. Corrupting the input or the stored operand changes the computed shift result, establishing integrity relevance.

conceptual assets.concept: Shift amount (distance) controlling how far the operand is shifted
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module takes the supplied shift amount and uses it to control the shift iteration or the barrel stages. Serial: on start "shifter.cnt <= shamt_i" and runtime decrements it ("shifter.cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(shifter.cnt) - 1)"); run/done derive from cnt ("shifter.run <= or_reduce_f(shifter.cnt)" and "shifter.done <= not or_reduce_f(shifter.cnt(...))"). Barrel: each stage tests "shamt_i(i) = '1'" to select bs_level movement. Corrupting shamt_i or the stored count changes the effective distance and so breaks correctness (integrity).

conceptual assets.concept: Shift result (the final shifted word delivered by the block)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module produces an explicit result output that must equal the implemented shift transformation. Serial: result leaves when captured by done_ff: "res_o <= shifter.sreg when (shifter.done_ff = '1') else (others => '0')". Barrel: result is formed from the registered level: "res_o <= bit_rev_f(bs_result) when (ctrl_i.ir_funct3(2) = '0') else bs_result" and "bs_result <= bs_level(...)" on the clock edge. Corrupting the stored source values or the gating (done_ff) changes the exported word, establishing an integrity requirement for the exit value and the registers that realize it.

conceptual assets.concept: Result-ready indicator (valid_o) that signals when the result is available
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module reports result readiness on valid_o using internal state. Serial: "valid_o <= shifter.busy and shifter.done". Barrel: "valid_o <= valid_cmd". An incorrect valid_o (stuck, flipped or forged) would cause consumers to accept or ignore results incorrectly; this outcome is implemented in RTL and thus integrity of the readiness signal is required. The ready decision is computed here (shifter.done, valid_cmd) and exported on the port valid_o.

conceptual assets.concept: Fill-bit selection for right shifts (arithmetic vs. logical fill)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The bit used to fill vacated positions on right shifts is computed from the operand sign and a control bit and is used by both implementations. Barrel: "bs_sign <= rs1_i(XLEN-1) and ctrl_i.ir_funct12(10) and valid_cmd" and bs_sign is used to populate upper bits when shifting (bs_level assignments). Serial: the right-shift update uses "(shifter.sreg(shifter.sreg'left) and ctrl_i.ir_funct12(10))" as the new MSB. Thus the selection of arithmetic (sign) versus zero fill is realized here (bs_sign / control inputs) and must have integrity to produce correct arithmetic/logical shift behavior.
